I wouldn't exactly say I stopped giving a fuck, I say that I started realizing the value things actually have. A lot of people go through life with an innate insecurity. They need validation. Whether it be through social interaction, financial gain, material acquisition, romantic entanglements, etc., they need to know that not only do they have value but others know they have value. For the most part, I am secure enough in myself that kind of status seeking has no appeal to me.

I live a simple life. I have a few good friends. I live modestly, but securely. I have a wife that I love and enjoy my time with. That is all I really need or want. Why desire crap that will only complicate my life? Why seek status if I would find status hollow? Why conspicuously consume if I don't actually care about the opinions of people that see me consuming? Once you realize what you actually want/need out of life all the other stuff seems pointless.

It's not that I stopped "giving a fuck", it's that I realized "giving a fuck" wasn't for me.

I was in school during the 80s and 90s. We took standardized test back then as earlier as kindergarten. I think the biggest difference between then and now is that everything is now based on the results, while back then it was just for data and overall trends (meta info). Changing how the data is used caused teachers to stop teaching everything and only teach what they know the student will be tested on, because the test is everything now.

The other issue is that we are treating schools like business branches. If I own and operate a bank and one of my branches is failing, I will tell them and hope they improve, if they don't I close the branch. We are doing the same with schools which should never be held to a business standard so removed from their purpose.
